items.query: Which probability must LogQ estimate for interaction-sampled minibatch negatives?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/In-batch nega.rationale: Identifies estimated batch sampling probability and its training-loss role.
excerpts:
The paper encodes queries and items with separate neural networks and scores a pair through their embedding inner product. Training approximates a full-corpus softmax using the items present in a minibatch as alternatives for each query. Rewards can weight the observed positive examples.

Because batch items follow a skewed interaction distribution, popular items appear disproportionately as negatives. The authors subtract the logarithm of an item's estimated batch sampling probability from its training logit. The corrected logits define the batch loss. The probability refers to how the training batch is sampled, and the method does not require a fixed item vocabulary.

The frequency estimator tracks the gap in global training steps between successive appearances of an item. A moving average estimates the mean gap, and its reciprocal estimates the item's batch sampling probability. Hash arrays store the latest occurrence and estimated gap without allocating a permanent entry for every item identifier.

Hash collisions combine appearances of different items and can overestimate frequency. The improved estimator maintains several independent hashings and uses the largest estimated gap. The global-step representation supports distributed parameter-server updates, while the moving average allows the estimate to adapt as the stream changes.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/HNSW construc.rationale: Explains construction controls and the connectivity available to later queries.

HNSW separates the breadth of insertion search from that of query search. During construction, efConstruction controls the candidate search used to establish connections. M controls the number of selected neighbors, subject to layer-specific limits.

The paper compares simply choosing the closest neighbors with a heuristic that also considers distances among candidate neighbors. 02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Hierarchical.rationale: Explains the insertion and query-search lifecycle.
excerpts:
HNSW stores vectors in a hierarchy of proximity graphs. Each inserted vector receives a randomly selected maximum level with an exponentially decreasing level distribution. Insertion searches from upper layers downward and connects the new vector to selected neighbors on its eligible layers.

Query search first performs greedy traversal on upper layers, using a small candidate set to find an entry point near the query. The bottom layer performs a broader search with a dynamic set of promising candidates. The final nearest candidates are returned from this ground-layer search. Upper and lower layers therefore use different search breadths.

items.query: Does LoRA make the pretrained weight matrix low rank, and why is the initial adaptation zero?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Frozen weight.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Frozen weights and low-rank updates in LoRA.
excerpts: LoRA freezes a pretrained weight matrix and represents its trainable update as a product of two smaller matrices. The forward computation sums the frozen matrix output and the low-rank update output for the same input. One factor is initialized randomly and the other to zero, so the initial update is zero. A scaling factor controls the contribution of the update while the rank sets the dimension of the adaptation factors.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/A zero initial.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Frozen weights and low-rank updates in LoRA distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: Initializing one LoRA factor to zero makes their product zero even though the other factor is random. The adapted layer therefore starts with the pretrained output and gains a trainable update during optimization. This initialization gives a functional starting-point guarantee. It does not mean both factors should be zero, because their gradient paths depend on the other factor's values.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/LoRA constrain.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Frozen weights and low-rank updates in LoRA distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: A pretrained matrix can remain full-rank while its task adaptation is represented by a low-rank increment. LoRA imposes the constraint on the change, not on the stored base transformation. This distinction explains how a compact adaptation can preserve a large model's original representation while restricting the additional degrees of freedom available for learning the new task.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Shared prefix.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Shared prefixes and copy-on-write in vLLM.
excerpts: Sequences generated from the same prompt can map their logical prompt blocks to the same physical KV-cache blocks. vLLM tracks references to shared blocks. When a sequence needs to modify a shared block, it allocates and copies a private block before writing. This block-level copy-on-write approach lets parallel sampling and beam search reuse common prefix state while storing divergent continuations separately.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/KV-cache shari.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Shared prefixes and copy-on-write in vLLM.

items.query: Why does watch-time weighting change a YouTube logistic ranker from an ordinary CTR predictor?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Watch-time we.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Watch-time weighting in YouTube ranking.
excerpts: YouTube's ranking model trains a logistic predictor on impressions. Clicked impressions receive weights equal to their observed watch time, while unclicked impressions receive unit weight. This changes the quantity represented by the fitted model from an ordinary click probability.

The authors relate the learned odds to expected watch time. Under their assumption that positive impressions form a small fraction of the data, those odds approximate the expected watch time of an impression. At inference, exponentiating the model's output produces the odds used for scoring. The approximation explicitly depends on the low-click-probability setting.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Watch-time-wei.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Watch-time weighting in YouTube ranking.
excerpts: Weighting clicked impressions by watch time changes the quantity estimated by a logistic model. Interpreting its odds as expected watch time relies on an approximation that becomes suitable when click probability is small. The scoring interpretation therefore includes an assumption about the data regime.

A sound explanation should state that assumption before presenting the score as a business quantity. The same weighting scheme applied in a different click regime would require revisiting the approximation rather than reusing the interpretation automatically.

items.query: Why does YouTube retrieval use earlier actions for a future-watch label and limit examples per user?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Temporal labe.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Temporal labels and user weighting in YouTube retrieval.
excerpts: The authors train candidate generation on watches from across YouTube rather than only watches produced by the recommender. They also generate a fixed number of examples per user so that highly active users do not dominate the objective.

For the prediction task, a randomly selected watch supplies the label, and only earlier actions supply its context. The authors report better results from predicting a future watch than from predicting a randomly held-out watch using the remaining history. The latter setup can expose later actions and discard the asymmetric order of consumption.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Prediction con.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Temporal labels and user weighting in YouTube retrieval distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: A future-event prediction task requires features that would have existed before the target event. Randomly removing one event while retaining later actions can disclose information unavailable at the intended decision time. A model can then perform well on the offline task for reasons that do not transfer to serving.
Temporal boundaries are therefore part of the task definition. They should be checked alongside labels and sampling before attributing a metric gain to a better representation.

excerpts: Sampling a fixed number of examples per user reduces the influence of users who generate many interactions. 02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Behavior-to-i.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Behavior-to-interest routing in MIND.
excerpts: MIND adapts capsule routing to aggregate variable-length behavior histories into interest vectors. It shares one bilinear mapping across behavior and interest capsules so that the resulting representations occupy a common vector space. Because shared mappings and identical routing initialization would produce identical interest capsules, the routing logits are initialized with Gaussian noise. Routing repeatedly computes assignment weights, aggregates the transformed behavior embeddings, and updates agreement between behavior and interest capsules.

Initialization cannot be assessed independently of parameter sharing; copying one routing component without the other can change the mechanism that keeps interest slots distinct.

items.query: What is asymmetric about Faiss distance computation with product-quantized database residuals?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Product quant.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Product quantization and asymmetric distance computation.
excerpts: Product quantization divides a vector into subvectors and quantizes each part with its own codebook. Concatenating the subvector codes produces a compact representation whose possible combinations greatly exceed the size of the individual codebooks.

Faiss uses query-dependent lookup tables to estimate distances to these codes. The query remains uncompressed while database residuals are quantized, which gives the computation its asymmetric form. Summing table entries avoids reconstructing every full database vector during scanning. The resulting distances remain estimates of distances to the original vectors.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Compact vector.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Product quantization and asymmetric distance computation distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: Product quantization stores a codebook assignment for each vector component group instead of retaining all original floating-point values. This saves per-vector storage, but distance computation now measures the query against a quantized representation. Close candidates can change order when their approximation errors differ.

The relevant trade-off includes recall and memory together. Code size alone cannot establish whether an index is suitable for a task, because relevance depends on which score distinctions the compression preserves.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Reference-rel.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Reference-relative preference optimization in DPO.
excerpts: DPO derives a policy objective from KL-regularized reward maximization and a preference model. Rewriting rewards in terms of policy-to-reference probability ratios makes a prompt-dependent partition function cancel in pairwise preference comparisons. The resulting loss directly trains the policy on preferred and dispreferred responses without fitting a separate reward model or running an RL optimization loop. The derivation relies on the assumed preference model and reference policy.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/DPO removes an.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Reference-relative preference optimization in DPO distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: Direct policy optimization avoids separately fitting and deploying a learned reward network inside an RL loop. It still relies on assumptions connecting observed pairwise preferences with an underlying ordering. Those assumptions shape the objective and its interpretation. Simpler optimization machinery therefore does not make the preference labels assumption-free or guarantee that they capture every desired behavior.

items.query: How does GRPO construct an outcome advantage without training a value model?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Group-relativ.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Group-relative advantages in GRPO.
excerpts: GRPO samples several outputs for the same question and estimates a baseline from their rewards rather than training a value model. For outcome supervision, it subtracts the group's mean reward and divides by the group standard deviation, applying the resulting advantage to tokens in each output. Its objective includes clipped policy-ratio terms and reference-policy regularization. The paper also explores process rewards, which assign feedback to intermediate reasoning steps.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Removing the c.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Group-relative advantages in GRPO distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: GRPO avoids maintaining a learned value model by estimating relative advantages from a group of sampled answers. It still needs to generate and score those answers. The resulting efficiency depends on model sizes, group size, response length, and reward computation. Removing one network reduces a specific resource requirement rather than making reinforcement learning inexpensive regardless of rollout workload.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Group-relative.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Group-relative advantages in GRPO distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: Subtracting a group's mean reward identifies responses that perform better or worse than their peers. If every sampled response receives the same reward, that group provides no relative ordering signal, and its standard deviation also needs numerical handling. This makes prompt difficulty and verifier discrimination relevant to training. Group comparison cannot manufacture useful preference evidence from identical observed rewards.

items.query: How do DPR in-batch negatives and a BM25 hard negative contribute different training alternatives?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Negative pass.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Negative passage selection in DPR.
excerpts: DPR optimizes the negative log probability of a positive passage against selected negative passages. The paper considers random corpus passages, high-ranked BM25 passages without the answer, and positives belonging to other questions. In-batch negatives reuse passage embeddings across the batch, creating a matrix of question-passage scores. The reported best training setup combines these in-batch gold passages with a BM25 negative.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Hard negatives.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Negative passage selection in DPR distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: Random passages often differ visibly from a positive, while high-ranked lexical negatives can share many query terms. The negative selection rule therefore shapes which distinctions receive a training signal. Reusing batch positives makes computation efficient, but it does not automatically provide the same learning problem as lexically confusable negatives. Training comparisons should describe both the sampler and the objective.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/A passage posi.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Negative passage selection in DPR distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: In-batch training treats other questions' passages as alternatives presumed negative for the current question. That assumption can fail when questions overlap or several passages answer the same need. Efficient score reuse does not establish label exclusivity. Examining the construction of question-passage pairs is therefore necessary before interpreting every off-diagonal score as evidence of irrelevant content.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Interleaved r.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Interleaved reasoning and external actions in ReAct.
excerpts: ReAct interleaves language reasoning with task-specific actions and observations. Reasoning can decompose a question, track progress, extract information, and reformulate a search after an observation. For question answering and fact verification, the paper provides Wikipedia search, lookup, and finish actions and manually composed few-shot trajectories. It notes that this deliberately limited retrieval interface is weaker than contemporary lexical or neural retrievers, because it is designed to require explicit interactive search.

excerpts: Interactive research gains value when external evidence changes what the agent does next. A failed search can motivate reformulation, and a discovered fact can narrow a remaining question. Merely issuing tools in a predetermined sequence does not demonstrate this adaptation. Inspecting how later actions depend on observations helps determine whether the loop is using evidence or only decorating an existing plan.

items.query: What decision separates a predefined workflow from an agent, and what costs come with added autonomy?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Predefined wo.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Predefined workflows and model-directed agents.
excerpts: The article distinguishes workflows, whose orchestration follows predefined code paths, from agents that dynamically direct their process and tool use. It recommends starting with the simplest adequate design and adding complexity when outcomes justify it. Workflows suit decomposable, well-defined tasks, while agents offer flexibility for open-ended paths. The article identifies increased latency, cost, and compounding errors as considerations for autonomous systems.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Agent autonomy.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Predefined workflows and model-directed agents distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: A system's autonomy depends on who chooses its next steps and tools. A language model inside a fixed pipeline does not automatically make that pipeline an autonomous agent. This distinction helps describe capabilities concretely: identify the decisions delegated to the model and those enforced by code. The same model can participate in systems with very different control boundaries.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Extra agent st.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Predefined workflows and model-directed agents distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: More model calls and tool decisions consume time and resources and introduce additional failure opportunities. Their value should be assessed through task outcomes under an explicit budget. A flexible loop may be justified for unpredictable research paths while a fixed workflow suffices elsewhere. Architecture complexity is consequently a hypothesis about improved performance, not evidence of improvement by itself.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Irrelevant ci.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Irrelevant citations and joint passage support in ALCE.
excerpts: ALCE's citation precision identifies citations that do not contribute support to a generated statement. Its procedure considers whether a cited passage supports the statement alone or whether removing it leaves the other cited passages sufficient. This accommodates statements requiring combined evidence from several passages. The paper presents precision alongside citation recall so that a fully cited answer can still be assessed for unnecessary or irrelevant references.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Joint support.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Irrelevant citations and joint passage support in ALCE.
excerpts: Some statements require evidence distributed across several passages. Demanding that every citation independently establish the complete claim can wrongly reject useful partial support. Conversely, adding irrelevant references can inflate apparent coverage. A citation assessment should examine whether the set supports the statement and whether each member contributes, reflecting the distinction between coverage and precision.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/At-least-one.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for At-least-one success and repeated reliability.
excerpts: The article distinguishes the probability of at least one successful attempt among k trials from the probability that every one of those trials succeeds. More attempts can improve the former while making the latter requirement harder. It discusses coding and customer-facing workflows as examples where these measures answer different questions. At one trial the measures coincide, while larger trial counts reveal the difference between finding a success and delivering it consistently.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Retry success.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for At-least-one success and repeated reliability.
excerpts: A task solved once after many attempts may demonstrate capability while offering poor reliability for a user expecting one correct delivery. At-least-one-success and all-trials-success metrics expose this difference. Comparisons need an explicit retry budget and selection rule. Otherwise additional attempts can make a system appear better while hiding the cost and inconsistency experienced in ordinary use.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Term saturati.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Term saturation and length scaling in BM25.
excerpts: The book introduces BM25 as a probabilistic scoring scheme sensitive to term frequency and document length. Its term-frequency component increases with occurrences while saturating, controlled by a tuning parameter. Another parameter controls scaling by document length relative to average collection length. Setting the length parameter to zero removes that normalization; setting it to one gives full length scaling in the presented formulation.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/BM25 frequency.rationale: This atomic record supplies a premise or qualification for the requested Term saturation and length scaling in BM25 distinction, but not all requested details.
excerpts: Under BM25, additional occurrences of a term give diminishing increments rather than an indefinitely linear score increase. The saturation parameter adjusts that response, while the length parameter addresses a different effect. Separating these roles makes tuning interpretable: rewarding repeated query terms and compensating for long documents are related in the formula but remain distinct scoring decisions.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Rank-based co.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Rank-based combination with reciprocal rank fusion.
excerpts: Reciprocal rank fusion sums a reciprocal contribution from each system's rank for a document, using an added constant to moderate the influence of very high positions. The method combines rankings without requiring comparable raw retrieval scores or training examples. The authors fix the constant at 60 after a pilot investigation and retain it for subsequent validation. Their reported improvements concern the particular TREC and LETOR combinations studied.

Fusion preserves ordering evidence while changing what information is available to the combination rule. Its suitability therefore depends on whether relative ranks provide enough signal for the task, and should be assessed on the combined candidate set.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Moment estima.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Moment estimation and bias correction in Adam.
excerpts: Adam maintains exponentially weighted estimates of the gradient's first moment and uncentered second moment. It uses these estimates to adapt updates and includes corrections for the bias introduced by initializing the accumulators to zero. The book compares these choices with momentum and RMSProp. It also notes that learning-rate adjustment can still be needed rather than treating the suggested defaults as universally sufficient.

That correction does not address class imbalance, dataset sampling bias, or bias in predictions toward a subgroup. These uses of the word bias refer to different quantities. Explaining the accumulator initialization makes the optimizer claim precise and avoids attributing unrelated statistical protections to Adam.

items.query: Why is dropout not independent training of every possible subnetwork?

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Dropout as sh.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Dropout as shared-subnetwork training.
excerpts: Dropout samples binary masks that remove input or hidden units during training. Each sampled subnetwork inherits parameters from the same underlying network. Training takes gradient steps for sampled masks rather than independently fitting every possible subnetwork. The book compares this with bagging while emphasizing shared parameters and the fact that only a small fraction of the possible subnetworks can be explicitly sampled.

02-Zettelkasten/Permanent/Dropout subnet.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Dropout as shared-subnetwork training.
excerpts: Dropout creates many possible masked computation paths while storing one shared parameter collection. Updating a sampled path changes parameters also used by other paths. Its ensemble analogy therefore differs from independently training separate networks to convergence. Parameter sharing is what makes the construction feasible, and it also limits how literally the subnetworks can be treated as independent ensemble members.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Pairwise inte.rationale: This record supplies the requested mechanism or distinction for Pairwise interaction parameters in factorization machines.
excerpts: A second-order factorization machine combines a global bias, linear feature terms, and pairwise feature interactions. Each feature has a latent factor vector, and the coefficient for a pair is the inner product of its two factor vectors. The interaction term also multiplies the corresponding feature values. Factor dimensionality is a model hyperparameter; the model does not allocate an independently learned coefficient to every feature pair.

excerpts: A small latent dimension constrains interaction coefficients to share a compact representation. Increasing dimension permits a richer pattern of pairwise relationships while adding parameters. Under sparse observations, added capacity may exceed the evidence available for estimation. Factor dimension is therefore a statistical capacity choice as well as a memory and computation setting.

This avoids explicitly enumerating every feature pair. Prediction has complexity linear in both feature count and factor dimension. For sparse feature vectors, the sums need only traverse nonzero values, so the cost depends on active features rather than the full vocabulary of possible features.

This distinction matters when explaining why a sparse feature model can represent many interactions while avoiding explicit quadratic enumeration at prediction time.
